newsitem.title: JAPAN: Moody's sees slow recovery for Japan builders.
newsitem.headline: Moody's sees slow recovery for Japan builders.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Monday the recovery of Japanese construction companies is expected to be slow, pressuring ratings in the sector.
Moody's said in a report that prolonged weakness of Japan's private construction market and the expected slowdown in public construction investment would hamper the sector's recovery.
Some companies continue to suffer from asset quality problems, leading to delays in the restoration of their balance sheets, it added.
Moody's also said the Japanese government's cost-reduction programme may further restrain the margins of contractors in an increasingly competitive market.
"Further delays in problem asset disposal and debt reaction will have a negative rating implication," it added.
Moody's rated the long-term debt and categorised the 11 Japanese general construction firms into three groups according to their risk profile.
The first group is comprised of Kajima Corp, rated A2, Obayashi Corp, rated Baa1, Taisei Corp, rated A3, and Shimizu Corp, rated A2.

The four major general contractors may face greater downward pressure on their ratings if they fail to improve their profitability, reduce their debt or manage to lower their existing exposure, Moody's said.
The second group consists of Maeda Corp, rated Baa3, Nishimatsu Construction Co Ltd 1820 T, rated A3, Toda Corp, rated Ba1, and Penta-Ocean Construction Co Ltd , rated Ba2, Moody's said.

It is expected that the companies' relatively sound financial profiles will keep their debt-protection measures within the appropriate parameters for each respective rating category over the intermediate term, Moody's said.
Fujita Corp, rated Ba3, Hazama Corp, rated B2, and Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd, rated B1, make up the third group.
It added that resolution of their problems and their financial flexibility to refinance maturing debts would be the key factors determining their ratings.
